sentences.en: Long ago, before the first song, the world was dark and silent.
sentences.editor: kroti muya montafama kroti li una-ne lira li vemi po ke narvosan ata lasosan.
sentences.spec: Kroti muya montafama, kroti li una-ne lira, li vemi po ka narvosan ata lasosan.
editor_checked: error slot: “li” cannot be placed in the clause template: expected the VERB.
error slot: “li” cannot be placed in the clause template: expected the VERB.
sentences.editor_back: ago: many year before the 1st song the world PAST is(now) dark and silent
sentences.spec_back: ago: many year before the 1st song the world PAST is dark and silent
cites: 2.1:G55 kroti + measure, no article = ago (muya montafama, many years ago)
1.2:G24 a time phrase opens the clause, comma
gaps: Ordinals: numbers rule J says ordinals 'await separate policy', but 2.1:G49 uses una-ne krono; una-ne lira extends that one example.
Two time phrases open the clause; FRAME is one slot and 1.0:G16 says one word per slot.

sentences.en: The goddess of light lived beyond the stars, and she was very lonely.
sentences.editor: li devi de lumi po bioba ultra li veluri, ata saivo po ke ruli pagonasan.
sentences.spec: Li devi de lumi po bioba ultra li veluri, ata saivo po ke ruli pagonasan.
sentences.editor_back: the goddess of light PAST live beyond the star.PL and he/she PAST is(now) very without a place
sentences.spec_back: the goddess of light PAST live beyond the star.PL and he/she PAST is(now) very without a place
cites: 1.2:G27 X de Y: the goddess of light
gaps: 'lonely' has no exact word: pagonasan is glossed 'without a place, homeless, family-less, lonely'.

sentences.en: One night she saw a small fire on a mountain.
sentences.editor: una nullo saivo po vimova baba mellinasan faru su baba monru.
sentences.spec: Una nullo, saivo po vimova baba mellinasan faru su baba monru.
editor_checked: error slot: “saivo” cannot be placed in the clause template: expected the VERB.
sentences.editor_back: 1 night he/she PAST see a small fire on a mountain
sentences.spec_back: 1 night he/she PAST see a small fire on a mountain
cites: 1.2:G27 example 'Nullo de deyaapo, maivo po ne somusia': a noun phrase of time may open the clause
1.2:G24 comma after an opening time phrase

sentences.en: Beside the fire sat a young singer named Dorin, and he was singing about the sea.
sentences.editor: silda li faru po semnesia baba yanbanasan lirayo nolesan Dorin, ata saivo po roni lirala [about] li sevu.
sentences.spec: Baba yanbanasan lirayo raho gome nolenia Dorin, po semnesia silda li faru, ata saivo po roni lirala lirari de li sevu.
editor_checked: error 1.2:G26: “semnesia” is followed by two bare noun phrases (“baba yanbanasan lirayo”, “nolesan Dorin”), but only give-type verbs take two. Join them with a preposition, or make one a de phrase.
sentences.editor_back: beside the fire PAST sit a young singer named Dorin and he/she PAST PROG sing the sea
sentences.spec_back: a young singer who PASS name Dorin PAST sit beside the fire and he/she PAST PROG sing song.PL of the sea
cites: 1.0:G21 a raho clause that does not end the sentence is closed by a comma
grammar.slots[14] gome (+ verb): passive, 'who is named'
1.2:G30 'about' is de, with an object after the verb (lirari de li sevu)
gaps: English locative inversion ('Beside the fire sat …') has no Liraasa counterpart; the clause keeps SUBJECT … VERB order.

sentences.en: His song was so beautiful that the stars began to weep.
sentences.editor: saivo de lira po ke tonsi vanisan fime li veluri po hiro [weep].
sentences.spec: Saivo de lira po ka tonsi vanisan fime li veluri hiro timruta.
editor_checked: error slot: “fime” opens a clause, and the clause has no verb (“veluri” is not a verb form; its verb is veluva).
sentences.editor_back: his/her song PAST is(now) so beautiful that the star.PL PAST begin to
sentences.spec_back: his/her song PAST is so beautiful that the star.PL begin to shed tears
cites: 1.2:G27 a pronoun before de is the owner
2.2:G62 tonsi + adjective … fime clause = so … that
0.8:R6 fime inherits the tense: no po

sentences.en: "Who is singing?" asked the goddess.
sentences.editor: li devi po masuma: “ki-nela roni lirala ki?”
sentences.spec: Li devi po masuma: “Ki-nela roni lirala ki?”
sentences.editor_back: the goddess PAST ask who PROG sing Q
sentences.spec_back: the goddess PAST ask who PROG sing Q
cites: 2.2:G60 a ki-word may open the question; it may end in ki
gaps: How a quotation is punctuated (colon, quotation marks) is shown in 0.8:G4's example but not stated.

sentences.en: The moon answered, "Only a child of the village; do not go to him."
sentences.editor: li luno po relsira: “doli baba linu de li vila. ne pagopa ala saivo.”
sentences.spec: Li luno po relsira: “Doli baba linu de li vila. Ne pagopa ala saivo!”
sentences.editor_back: the moon PAST answer only a child of the village NOT go to he/she
sentences.spec_back: the moon PAST answer only a child of the village NOT go to he/she
cites: 0.8:G3 an answer may be a fragment
1.0:G1 doli scopes over the constituent that follows

sentences.en: But the goddess did not listen, and she came down to the mountain.
sentences.editor: nara li devi po ne lenila, ata saivo po nevrania ala li monru.
sentences.spec: Nara li devi po ne lenila, ata saivo po nevrania ala li monru.
sentences.editor_back: but the goddess PAST NOT hear and he/she PAST descend to the mountain
sentences.spec_back: but the goddess PAST NOT hear and he/she PAST descend to the mountain
cites: 0.8:G2 ne after the tense, before the verb
gaps: Can nara open a sentence that continues the one before? 1.2:G25 settles this only for oro (and the checker asks the same of ata). Options: (a) allow nara, like oro; (b) require narli (nevertheless) sentence-initially.

sentences.en: She gave the singer a silver ring and said, "Sing for me every night."
sentences.editor: saivo po donuda baba vanajubasan rinba ala li lirayo ata po senosia: “lirala vobi maivo toda nullo.”
sentences.spec: Saivo po donuda baba vanajubasan rinba ala li lirayo ata po senosia: “Lirala vobi maivo rada nullo.”
sentences.editor_back: he/she PAST give a silvery ring to the singer and PAST speak sing for I all night
sentences.spec_back: he/she PAST give a silvery ring to the singer and PAST speak sing for I each night
cites: 0.8:G3 a repeated subject may be omitted in coordinated clauses
2.0:G39 vanajuba is a headword: its adjective vanajubasan

sentences.en: Dorin sang for her three times, and each time the darkness grew smaller.
sentences.editor: Dorin po lirala vobi saivo tressa-krono, ata rada-krono li narvo po loya kasi mellinasan.
sentences.spec: Dorin po lirala vobi saivo tressa-krono, ata rada-krono li narvo po loya kasi mellinasan.
sentences.editor_back: Dorin PAST sing for he/she tressa times and each time the darkness PAST become more small
sentences.spec_back: Dorin PAST sing for he/she tressa times and each time the darkness PAST become more small
cites: 1.2:G34 rada-krono = each time; it may open its clause

sentences.en: The king of the city heard about the singer and wanted the ring for himself.
sentences.editor: li tarnuregna de li cilni po lenila li telne de li lirayo ata po desida li rinba vobi saivo sela.
sentences.spec: Li tarnuregna de li cilni po lenila li telne de li lirayo ata po desida li rinba vobi saivo sela.
sentences.editor_back: the king of the city PAST hear the story of the singer and PAST want the ring for he/she oneself
sentences.spec_back: the king of the city PAST hear the story of the singer and PAST want the ring for he/she oneself
cites: 1.2:G30 'about' is de with an object after the verb
gaps: 'hear about X' needs an object noun the English does not have (telne, story, is supplied). 1.2:G30 covers verbs of saying only. Options: (a) extend G30 to verbs of perceiving and knowing (hear, know, think) with a stock object; (b) allow VERB de NP directly after these verbs.

sentences.en: He sent seven soldiers with swords to the mountain.
sentences.editor: saivo po silbesia seta dokrayori ko tisebitivuri ala li monru.
sentences.spec: Saivo po silbesia seta dokrayori ko tisebitivuri ala li monru.
sentences.editor_back: he/she PAST send 7 soldier.PL with sword.PL to the mountain
sentences.spec_back: he/she PAST send 7 soldier.PL with sword.PL to the mountain
cites: 1.0:G20 tisebitivu (sword) is a listed derivation; dokrayo (soldier) is listed (2.3)
ala = toward (a place, not a recipient: 1.2:G26 does not apply)

sentences.en: If the moon had not warned him, the singer would have died.
sentences.editor: si li luno po noma ne nengania saivo, li lirayo po viki daigoda.
sentences.spec: Si li luno po noma ne nengania saivo, li lirayo po viki daigoda.
sentences.editor_back: if the moon PAST COUNTERFACT NOT warn him/her the singer PAST would die
sentences.spec_back: if the moon PAST COUNTERFACT NOT warn him/her the singer PAST would die
cites: 1.0:G6 noma = contrary to fact; 'would have' = po viki in a consequence clause

sentences.en: The singer hid behind a great tree and waited until morning.
sentences.editor: li lirayo po helviha nazru baba [great] larbo ata po sulnosia tuni merno.
sentences.spec: Li lirayo po helviha nazru baba mellisan larbo ata po sulnosia tuni li merno venreva.
sentences.editor_back: the singer PAST hide behind a tree and PAST wait until morning
sentences.spec_back: the singer PAST hide behind a large tree and PAST wait until the morning come
gaps: tuni is shown only before a clause; whether 'tuni li merno' (until morning) is grammar is not said.

sentences.en: The soldiers could not find him, because the forest protected him.
sentences.editor: li dokrayori ne povi navdinia saivo, kasa li larbopago po sasvasia saivo.
sentences.spec: Li dokrayori po ne povi navdinia saivo, kasa li larbopago sasvasia saivo.
sentences.editor_back: the soldier.PL NOT can find him/her because the forest PAST protect him/her
sentences.spec_back: the soldier.PL PAST NOT can find him/her because the forest protect him/her
cites: 0.8:G2 / 1.0:G15 ne before the modal negates the ability
0.8:R6 kasa inherits the tense: no po

sentences.en: Then the goddess made the king sleep for a hundred years.
sentences.editor: krotiata li devi po vaku li tarnuregna somusia centa montafama.
sentences.spec: Krotiata li devi po vaku li tarnuregna somusia centa montafama.
sentences.editor_back: then the goddess PAST CAUSE the king sleep 100 year
sentences.spec_back: then the goddess PAST CAUSE the king sleep 100 year
cites: 1.0:G14 vaku ACTOR VERB; tense belongs to the main clause only
2.1:G55 a bare measure after the object = duration

sentences.en: What a beautiful night it was!
sentences.editor: li nullo po ke ki-modo vanisan!
sentences.spec: Li nullo po ka ki-modo vanisan!
sentences.editor_back: the night PAST is(now) how beautiful
sentences.spec_back: the night PAST is how beautiful
cites: 2.2:G61 ki-modo + adjective without final ki = an exclamation
copula ka with po keeps the past tense
gaps: 2.2:G61's ki-eli + noun ('Ki-eli vanisan nullo!', what a beautiful night) has no verb, so it cannot carry 'it was': past exclamatives must use ki-modo with a copula.

sentences.en: Since then, the singer and the goddess sing to each other across the sky.
sentences.editor: da ola-krono li lirayo ata li devi lirala transa li navu fuyi.
sentences.spec: Da ola-krono, li lirayo ata li devi lirala transa li navu fuyi.
sentences.editor_back: from then the singer and the goddess sing through the sky each other
sentences.spec_back: from then the singer and the goddess sing through the sky each other
cites: da = from, before the correlative ola-krono (then)
grammar.clause_template [ADJUNCTS] [fuyi]: the reciprocal follows the adjuncts
gaps: 'since then': sige (since) takes only a clause, and no ruling gives 'since + time word'. Options: (a) da + correlative (from then), as used here; (b) sige + correlative (sige ola-krono).

sentences.en: Perhaps you can hear them when the moon is full.
sentences.editor: taivo povi lenila saivori poye kube li luno ke fulesan.
sentences.spec: Kube li luno ke fulesan, taivo povi lenila saivori poye.
sentences.editor_back: you can hear them maybe when the moon is(now) full
sentences.spec_back: when the moon is(now) full you can hear them maybe
cites: kube = when (subordinate), opening with a comma
1.0:G22 'Perhaps, …' is written with the clause-final poye
copula ke: the full moon is a passing state

sentences.en: May their song protect you always.
sentences.editor: saivori de lira sasvasia taivo toda-krono pifu.
sentences.spec: Toda-krono, saivori de lira sasvasia taivo pifu.
sentences.editor_back: their song protect you always wish
sentences.spec_back: always their song protect you wish
cites: 2.1:G48 pifu with any subject is the blessing form
1.2:G24 a time correlative opens its clause
1.2:G27 a pronoun before de is the owner
gaps: A time word may close its clause (1.2:G24) and an attitude word must close it (1.0:G22): their order when both close a clause ('… taivo toda-krono pifu') is not stated.
